utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm Dr. [your name]. I understand you've been having burning when you pass urine since yesterday. I'm sorry you're uncomfortable. Let me ask you a few questions about it so I can work out the best treatment for you.
reply: It stings and burns, especially at the end when I wee. It feels just like my last UTI. I've been going all the time — every half hour — but only a little comes out each time. I have to rush.

utterance: Thanks, that's really helpful. A few more things I need to check. Have you noticed any blood in your urine, or any unusual smell or cloudiness?
reply: It's a bit cloudy and smells, but I haven't seen any blood.

awards.label: Colour of the urine or any visible blood

utterance: And have you had any pain in your lower tummy, in your back or sides, or up high in your belly area?
reply: No, nothing in my back. Just a bit of an ache low down in my tummy, and just the low ache above my bladder. Nothing else.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Pain in the back or sides (loins)
Red flag excluded: Abdominal pain beyond a low ache

utterance: Have you had any fever, chills, or felt shivery or achey at all?
reply: No, no fevers or shivers. I feel fine apart from this.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Fever, sweats, chills or shaking

reply: No, I'm eating normally. Haven't been sick.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Nausea, vomiting or feeling generally unwell

utterance: Good, that's reassuring. Is there any vaginal discharge, itch, or a change in how things smell down there? And any pain or discomfort during sex?
reply: No, nothing like that. No pain or discomfort during sex either.

utterance: Could you be pregnant at all? When was your last period?
reply: No, I don't think I could be pregnant. My last period was about two weeks ago, and it was normal.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Whether she could be pregnant

utterance: You mentioned this feels like your last UTI — how long ago was that, and how many UTIs have you had in the past, roughly? Have you had any with a fever or kidney infection before?
reply: It's been about a day and a half since the symptoms started. I had one UTI about two years ago, that's it — nothing else. I don't have any kidney or bladder problems.

awards.label: How long the symptoms have been present

utterance: Thanks. Just a couple more. Have you recently started a new sexual partner, or had any changes in that area? And do you use anything like spermicides, diaphragms, or condoms?
reply: No, I've been with the same boyfriend for about a year, just him. We don't use condoms because I'm on the pill.

utterance: Any other medical conditions I should know about, or anything else you're taking — any medicines, supplements, or over-the-counter things? And do you have any allergies to any medicines, especially antibiotics?
reply: No, I'm not allergic to anything that I know of. I'm on the combined oral contraceptive pill, that's it. I don't take any other medicines, supplements, or over-the-counter things.

finding: Soft abdomen. Mild suprapubic tenderness. No guarding or rebound. No masses.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance: Everything points to a simple bladder infection — the urine test shows signs of infection, and you're otherwise well with no fever. I've started you on an antibiotic called trimethoprim, one tablet a day for 3 days. Most people feel a lot better within a day or two.
reply: Thanks, I'll take it. I hope it works. I need to get back to work soon.

utterance: A few important things to remember. Finish the full 3-day course even if you feel better, so the infection clears completely. Keep drinking plenty of water, and passing urine when you need to — don't hold it.
reply: I'll make sure to finish the course. I'll drink lots of water and go when I need to. I hope it clears up quickly so I can get back to work.

utterance: You should feel better within 1 to 2 days. If you're not improving after 48 hours, or if you start to feel worse, please come back. And come back — or go to the emergency department — straight away if you develop any of these: a fever or chills, pain in your back or sides, feeling sick or vomiting, or blood in your urine.
reply: I'll keep an eye on it. If it doesn't get better, I'll come back. Thanks for helping.

utterance: I've also sent a sample of your urine to the lab to check exactly what's causing it and which antibiotics work best. If that result shows the antibiotic isn't the right one, I'll contact you to switch it. So just keep your phone handy over the next couple of days.
reply: I'll make sure to keep my phone handy. If they need to change the antibiotic, I'll be ready.

awards.label: Reasonable differential: Urethritis from a sexually transmitted infection
